chunks.text: A fraction represents a part of a whole or any number of equal parts. It is written as a numerator over a denominator separated by a fraction line.

In a fraction, the top number is the Numerator (how many equal parts are selected), and the bottom number is the Denominator (the total number of equal parts that make up the whole). The denominator can never be zero.

Equivalent fractions are different fractions that name the exact same amount or value (for example, 1/2, 2/4, and 4/8 are all equivalent). You can find equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing both the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.
A ratio is a comparison of two quantities indicating how many times one value contains another. Ratios can be expressed as a:b, as a fraction a/b, or with words 'a to b'.

misconceptions.correction: A larger denominator means the whole is divided into more smaller pieces! For example, 1/8 is smaller than 1/2 because splitting a whole into 8 pieces produces smaller pieces than splitting into 2.
